props.gloss_en: Grace after Meals is from the Torah: 'and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless' (Deut 8:10)
'and you shall bless' -- that is the blessing 'who feeds'
the tanna kama: 'the Lord your God' -- that is the zimmun blessing
'for the land' -- that is the blessing of the land
'the good' -- that is 'who builds Jerusalem'; and so it says 'this good mountain and the Lebanon' (Deut 3:25)
the tanna kama: 'which He gave you' -- that is 'who is good and does good'
Rebbi: but the zimmun blessing is derived from 'magnify the Lord with me' (Ps 34:4)
Rebbi: 'who is good and does good' -- they instituted it at Yavne
Rebbi: whence [a blessing] before [eating]? 'which He gave you' -- from when He gave [it] to you
R' Yitzchak: it is unnecessary -- 'and He will bless your bread and your water' (Ex 23:25): do not read uveirakh but uvareikh; and when is it called bread? before one eats it
R' Natan: it is unnecessary -- 'for the people will not eat until he comes, for he blesses the sacrifice; afterwards those invited eat' (I Sam 9:13)
why so much [speech]? because women are talkative
Shmuel: in order to gaze at Saul's beauty
Shmuel's verse: 'from his shoulders upward he was taller than all the people' (I Sam 9:2)
R' Yochanan: because one reign does not touch its fellow even by a hairbreadth

R' Chiyya bar Nachmani in R' Yishmael's name: it is unnecessary -- it says 'for the good land which He gave you', and below it says 'and I will give you the tablets of stone and the Torah and the commandment' (Ex 24:12)
R' Meir: just as one blesses over the good, so one blesses over the bad
R' Meir's source: 'which the Lord your God gave you'
R' Meir: '[your] God' -- your Judge, in every judgment He judges you, whether a measure of good or a measure of calamity
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: it is unnecessary -- it says 'good', 'the good': 'good' is Torah, and so it says 'for I have given you a good teaching' (Prov 4:2)
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: 'the good' is the building of Jerusalem, and so it says 'this good mountain and the Lebanon'
the din R' Yitzchak's verse answers: a blessing is required BEFORE eating (the baraita's question, which his אינו צריך takes up)
R' Yitzchak's criterion: read uvareikh ('and bless your bread') -- bread requires a blessing
R' Yitzchak's bridge: when is it called 'bread'? before one eats it -- so the blessing over 'bread' is the blessing before eating
R' Meir's bridge: your Judge in every judgment He judges you, a measure of calamity included -- so the blessing to 'the Lord your God' extends to the bad
